claim: For the three-state hinge-graph \(p=\infty\) hardcore-SOS model on the Cayley tree of order \(k=3\), let \(\mu_1(\theta)\) be the translation-invariant splitting Gibbs measure corresponding to \(x=1\) and the large positive root \(y_1>2^{1/4}\) of \(\theta y^4-y^3+y-2\theta=0\), with \(0<\theta<1\). If \(\lambda(\theta)\) denotes the second-largest transition-matrix eigenvalue in absolute value, then \(\lambda(\theta)\le 1/3\) and therefore \(3\lambda(\theta)^2-1\le-2/3\). Both inequalities are sharp, with equality exactly at \(y_1=\sqrt2\) and \(\theta=1/\sqrt2\). Consequently the Kesten–Stigum sufficient non-extremality condition \(3\lambda(\theta)^2>1\) never holds anywhere on this large branch for \(0<\theta<1\). This does not assert extremality of \(\mu_1\); failure of the Kesten–Stigum sufficient test is not a converse theorem.
integrity: The proof is an exact algebraic reduction from the published boundary-law and transition-matrix formulas. Finite numerical evaluations are used only as consistency checks, not as proof.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns only the large \(x=1\) hinge-graph branch at \(k=3\) and \(0<\theta<1\).
Failure of the Kesten–Stigum sufficient non-extremality criterion does not prove extremality.
title: Sharp Kesten–Stigum gap on the large \(k=3\) hardcore-SOS branch
